title: Connect two people across apps
summary: One person shows a code or sends a link that names a per-encounter messaging identifier with its relays and a fresh challenge; the other scans it, proposes the relationship, and both issue a relationship credential to each other. Two existing registry tasks, no third party; completes offline when the proposal is shown back as a code.

inviter.description: Shows the code or sends the link that names its per-encounter messaging identifier, relays and challenge; accepts the proposal and issues a credential about the responder.

responder.description: Scans the code or opens the link; proposes the relationship and issues a credential about the inviter.

propose.description: The responder's proposal and the inviter's acceptance (its #response, naming the inviter's pairwise identifier). The proposal's id is the responder's fresh challenge and the threadId of every later document; ceremony.enactment is the inviter's challenge from the link. Sent to a relay named in the inviter's identifier, or shown back as a code when both are offline.

issue-inviter.description: The inviter's relationship credential about the responder, and the responder's receipt (its #response, carrying the digest of the credential as stored). Follows the acceptance; may travel with it.

issue-responder.description: The responder's relationship credential about the inviter, and the inviter's receipt. Follows the acceptance and does not wait for the inviter's credential; the two issue steps may cross.

sideEffects.rationale: Each party mints a credential about the other. Not compensatable by this ceremony; revocation is the issuer's own act.

exposure.rationale: Each issue step delivers credential material the other party retains, and each party issues on its own authority about a person present or named. enactmentPrivacy is shared because the two parties are meant to know they share this flow, and the pairwise identifiers already correlate the pair; the messaging identifiers are per encounter, so a leaked pair of credentials links one enactment and nothing beyond it.

org.real-life.rltp.note: The definition proposed in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1034 (three steps, 8 November 2026), kept here so DTGWG tooling and the test vector agree on one text. The flow is implemented in lib/src/shared-connect.ts and exercised by vectors/shared-connect.json. Until the registry publishes the definition, steps carry {enactment, step} and no definition or definitionDigest.
org.real-life.rltp.entry: A VTI trigger link on the shared origin: https://link.trustoverip.org/t#_from=<per-encounter peer DID with relays>&_id=<16-byte challenge, canonical base64url>&_exp=<epoch seconds>&_type=/vti/flow/shared-connect/0.1[&_label=<display name, code shown in person only>]. _from is a did:peer:2 or a long-form did:peer:4 with the relay as a service; _id is ceremony.enactment. A code shown in person expires within 10 minutes, a link sent in a message within 7 days.
org.real-life.rltp.identifiers: Two layers: a per-encounter messaging identifier (the peer DID in _from, the propose issuer; the only identifier a relay or an observer sees) and a pairwise relationship identifier (relationshipDid: an Ed25519 did:key or did:peer:0; it signs the credential and stays stable while the messaging identifier may change).
org.real-life.rltp.credential: Each issue carries a VC of types VerifiableCredential, DTGCredential and RelationshipCredential (plus EncounterCredential when the issuer's channel was scan or displayed) with credentialSubject {id: the other party's relationshipDid, ceremony: https://trusttasks.org/ceremony/shared-connect/0.1, challenge: the issuer's own challenge, enactmentBinding, channel}. enactmentBinding is a multibase multihash over the JCS canonicalization of {ceremony, challenges: [the two challenges, sorted]}, so a credential names both fresh values although ceremony.enactment carries only the inviter's.
org.real-life.rltp.offline: When neither side has a network the responder shows the signed proposal back as a code in a reconstruction form (_type=/vti/flow/shared-connect/0.1/back with rel, t, n, sig); the inviter rebuilds the propose document from it and verifies the proof. The remaining steps follow over any carrier.
org.real-life.rltp.freshness: The proposal is accepted within 10 minutes of its issuedAt and before the link's _exp; the acceptance within 10 minutes of its issuedAt; 60 seconds of clock tolerance in the document's favour. The issue steps have no window of their own: the credentials' timestamps are read as evidence, not as commands. No maxDuration is declared for this reason.
org.real-life.rltp.proofs: Step proofs are eddsa-jcs-2022 by the messaging identifier's authentication key (#key-1); credential proofs by the relationship identifier under assertionMethod, with the credential's @context repeated in the proof.
